cg.description: Altcoinist, The Trader In Your Pocket, is autonomous trading infrastructure for onchain markets. The platform combines execution, signal detection, and position management into one integrated system designed to reduce the manual effort required in active trading. The execution engine routes trades across 100+ decentralized exchanges. Signal intelligence aggregates onchain activity, social data, and market indicators to identify tokens showing confluence, where multiple data sources point in the same direction. Position management provides 24/7 monitoring of open trades with alerts for scaling, profit-taking, and risk management. These three layers are designed to function as a connected loop rather than standalone tools. Data from execution informs signal detection, signals guide position decisions, and position outcomes feed back into the system. This architecture supports the platform's long-term direction: an autonomous trading agent that can monitor markets, identify opportunities, and execute trades based on user-defined risk parameters. Altcoinist currently operates as a Telegram-based trading interface, with planned expansion to additional interfaces and integration.

adverseMentions.text: @Altcoinist I'm working on how to run my @Altcoinist account now that scans are public. Before, I would scan everything: new pairs I'm researching, gambles, conviction plays, rugs to avoid etc, because I shared the info in my tg. I stopped scanning as much now because I don't want to spam people, and don't want people to auto-buy rugs. I go fast, so I don't have time to add a thesis to every play, but that means a lot of my best plays haven't been scanned, like $WADDLES. I got in early, and should have scanned it so others could too, but I'd already scanned a ton of new pairs while gem hunting, and realized those scans were spamming followers' wallets. I didn't use the beta app until recently, so I didn't consider how it all worked. The last couple days I scanned the way I usually do, but there were a bunch of rugs and I feel bad about anyone who aped that doesn't know my trading style. It's a mix of HR/HR and long-term investments. TIBBIR is the perfect example. I took a big early risk on something with potential, but it was still speculative and had what a lot of traders thought of as red flags. I'm also upgrading my system with new tech. I'm still competing well enough, but I've never used FOMO and rarely check it, so that's a new world I need to integrate. There have been some plays I should never have entered had I checked the FOMO wallets.

basicFactQuestionLedger.question: What exact project or company does this account represent?
Who founded or co-founded the project? Return one person per answer.
Who currently leads or operates the project? Return one person and role per answer.
When was the project founded?
What live products or services does the project provide?
When did its product, protocol, or mainnet launch?
What is the project's official crypto token, if any?
Does the organization have a publicly traded equity or debt security distinct from any crypto token?
Which blockchain networks or chains does it run on?
What source-backed funding rounds or amounts has it raised?
Which named investors or backers are source-backed? Return one per answer.
Which material operating partners, counterparties, or product integrations are source-backed? Return one named relationship per answer and exclude rumors, proposals, and ended relationships.
Where is the official source code maintained?
What concrete, dated usage, revenue, volume, users, fees, TVL, or adoption metrics are public?
Which legal entity is responsible for the project?
What material legal or regulatory events are publicly documented, who are they attributed to, and what is each event's current stated status?

What material hacks, exploits, breaches, thefts, user losses, emergency pauses, or recovery outcomes are publicly documented? Return each event with an exact date, amount, attribution, current status, and direct source.
What formal governance process is documented?
Who has practical control through ownership, boards, voting power, admin keys, multisigs, or treasury authority?
What explicit related-party arrangements or conflicts of interest are disclosed?
What token allocation or supply disclosures are published?
What vesting, lockup, or unlock schedule is published?
What treasury assets, reports, wallets, or controls are disclosed?
Which independent security audits or reviews are published?
